concept.centerRule: Only explicit angel-language or a in Scripture identified named angel establishes angelic identity. Men, spirits, cherubim, seraphim, living creatures, heavenly armies, and hostile powers remain distinct unless a source makes the connection.

characterAnchors.label: Hagar
characterAnchors.note: Is found, questioned, directed, and addressed in two wilderness crises.

characterAnchors.label: Abraham
characterAnchors.note: Hears the LORD’s angel halt the binding of Isaac and repeat promise.

characterAnchors.label: Jacob
characterAnchors.note: Sees angels at Bethel and Mahanaim and later invokes the angel who redeemed him.

characterAnchors.label: Moses
characterAnchors.note: Meets the LORD’s angel at the bush and leads a people promised angelic guidance.

characterAnchors.label: Gideon
characterAnchors.note: Receives commission and recognizes the LORD’s angel after fire consumes the offering.

characterAnchors.label: Raphael
characterAnchors.note: Is sent to heal, guide, bind, present prayers, disclose his name, and return.

characterAnchors.label: Gabriel
characterAnchors.note: Stands in God’s presence and is sent to announce John and Jesus.

characterAnchors.label: Michael
characterAnchors.note: Restrains condemnation in Jude and leads angels against the dragon in Revelation.

characterAnchors.label: Jesus Christ / the Son of Man
characterAnchors.note: Is served by angels, teaches about them, sends them, and receives their worship.

characterAnchors.label: John
characterAnchors.note: Receives Revelation through angelic agents and is twice redirected when he attempts worship.

concept.throughline: Angels move through ancestral encounters, exodus memory, prophetic judgment, named missions, the life and teaching of Jesus, apostolic argument, conflict, worship, and Revelation’s final disclosures.

nodes.note: The LORD’s angel asks Hagar where she came from and where she is going, directs her return, names Ishmael, and the narrator closes with Hagar naming the LORD who spoke.
nodes.title: The LORD’s angel finds Hagar by the spring

nodes.note: The LORD’s angel calls from the sky, stops Abraham’s hand, speaks again after the ram is offered, and restates blessing in the LORD’s name.
nodes.title: The LORD’s angel stops Abraham and repeats the promise

nodes.note: The bush scene opens with the LORD’s angel in flame, then the LORD sees, God calls, and Moses hides his face from God before receiving his commission.
nodes.title: The LORD’s angel appears in the burning bush

nodes.note: The donkey sees the sword-bearing LORD’s angel before Balaam does; opened eyes expose the adversary, Balaam confesses, and his speech is restricted.
nodes.title: The LORD’s angel stands against Balaam

nodes.note: The LORD’s angel addresses Gideon, the narration shifts to the LORD speaking, fire consumes the offering, and Gideon fears after seeing the angel face to face.
nodes.title: The LORD’s angel calls Gideon and departs in fire

nodes.note: Manoah’s wife meets the LORD’s angel, calls him a man of God, receives the birth instruction twice, and watches the unnamed messenger ascend in altar flame.
nodes.title: The LORD’s angel announces Samson and ascends in flame

nodes.note: Pestilence reaches Jerusalem; the LORD tells the destroying angel to withdraw, David sees the angel, confesses, and builds an altar at Araunah’s threshing floor.
nodes.title: The destroying angel stops at Jerusalem

pivots.title: Follow the LORD’s angel

pivots.description: Trace guarding, sea crossing, land entry, judgment after the calf, and remembered exodus.

nodes.note: The angel of God and the cloud move from before Israel to behind the camp as the sea opens, Egypt enters, and Israel crosses on dry ground.
nodes.title: The angel of God moves behind Israel at the sea

nodes.note: God promises an angel to keep Israel on the way, commands attention to his voice because the divine name is in him, and connects his going with entry into the land.
nodes.title: An angel is sent before Israel with the divine name

nodes.note: Moses seeks atonement after the calf; the LORD answers with judgment, commands the journey, and says his angel will go before the people.
nodes.title: After the calf, God says his angel will go before

nodes.note: The LORD tells Moses to depart, promises to send an angel and drive out nations, yet says he will not go in Israel’s midst because of their stubbornness.

nodes.note: Moses’ message to Edom compresses Israel’s affliction, cry, divine hearing, a sent angel, and the exodus before requesting passage.

pivots.title: Follow the angel who goes before

pivots.description: Trace figures seen as men, messengers recognized late, and angels present without human recognition.
